statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail is 15% and remains below the watch threshold, while Stress stays elevated at 57% because a multi-decade-high long end, a $94 Brent risk premium and a sharp gold bid are all pressing against the equity bounce at once.
recommendation: The mapped policy state remains EA_ON, with a narrow flagged window from 13:30Z to 15:00Z covering the US cash open and the S&P Global flash PMI pair. The elevated Stress reading describes cross-asset conflict rather than observed one-way Nasdaq-100 structure: the overnight range was two-sided and retracements remain present in the current price path. A second, unflagged concentration point is the 19:00Z power hour on August monthly options expiry.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures firm about 0.6% into the cash open after a five-day slump, but a 4.65-4.69% 10-year and a sharp gold bid keep the bounce conditional.
body: NQ September futures trade near 29,450-29,510, roughly +0.5% to +0.7% against a 29,300.50 prior close, holding the upper half of a two-sided 29,274-29,539 overnight range after five consecutive losing sessions for the Nasdaq-100. The bounce is not confirmed across assets. The 10-year sits near 4.65-4.69% and the 30-year near 5.19% after a week in which the Treasury's decision to double long-dated buybacks to at least $4bn per operation failed to deliver sustained relief. Brent near $94 carries an Iran risk premium ahead of a Treasury press conference on Monday detailing measures to economically isolate Iran, and gold is up roughly 1.5% on the day, a combination that reads as hedging rather than a clean risk-on turn. Against that, VIX near 14.9 and down about 6%, together with uniformly positive megacap and semiconductor performance in the latest session, argue against a panic regime. No persistent one-way structure, shallow-pullback sequence or failed-retracement pattern is present in the observed price path, so Tail stays low at 15% while Stress is held elevated at 57%. The immediate checkpoints sit inside the current hour: the 13:30Z cash open and the 13:45Z S&P Global flash PMI pair, whose prices and new-orders components can transmit straight back into the long end. Later in the session, August monthly options expiry concentrates closing flow into the 19:00Z power hour, and US index futures then halt for the weekend from 21:00Z. The week ahead stacks Nvidia's Q2 fiscal 2027 results and the GDP second estimate and July PCE report on August 26, followed by the Jackson Hole symposium on August 27-29.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is partial: six hourly assessments are available (01:00Z, 06:00Z, 07:00Z, 08:00Z, 11:00Z and 12:00Z) and the remaining eighteen clock-hours have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across the available slots Tail stayed tightly contained between 12% and 14% with a green mapped state throughout, Stress decayed from 59% to 53% through the quiet overnight session before ticking back to 56% as the European morning brought gold, Brent and the long end back into focus, and Confidence improved from 83% to a 86-87% plateau as more of the session's evidence became verifiable.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds watch level for the 13:00Z and 14:00Z hours, which contain the US cash open and the S&P Global flash PMI pair, then decays back toward the session baseline through the New York afternoon on the assumption that price discovery stays orderly and the long end holds its range. A modest step up is carried into the 19:00Z power hour because August monthly options expiry concentrates closing and roll flow, though such swings are typically two-sided rather than one-way. From 21:00Z US index futures are scheduled to halt for the weekend, so the final sixteen slots carry a closed-market floor: Tail falls to 6-8% because no tradable price path exists, Stress sits in the moderate band reflecting weekend headline exposure through the Iran sanctions and oil channel ahead of Monday's Treasury press conference, and Confidence decays from 72% to 63% purely as a function of distance from the last verified market observation.
